- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3), model underestimates; adjust upward by 3–7% if recent price is falling.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak for 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a strong trend, model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 1–3% for 5–7 days post-peak.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates in early 2025 (Q1) when sentiment is mixed; add 1–3% to forecast for first 10 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.6, 1.0, 0.3, 1.0), model tends to lag; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days to catch momentum.
